raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/55635.

Install the pinned AWS EFA userspace runtime when building the vLLM image with
`INSTALL_KV_CONNECTORS=true`. This provides the libfabric runtime required by
NIXL's bundled `LIBFABRIC` plugin and is expected to support the Mooncake
TransferEngine path as well.

The EFA installer automatically selects the appropriate packages for `amd64`
or `arm64`, allowing both platforms to use the same Dockerfile implementation.
Kernel modules and host limit configuration are deliberately excluded from the
container installation and remain the responsibility of the host.

The installation:

- Pins AWS EFA installer version `1.50.0` and verifies its SHA-256 checksum.
- Installs the EFA userspace stack without kernel modules or host limit changes.
- Verifies that `/opt/amazon/efa/bin/fi_info` is executable.
- Verifies that NIXL's `libplugin_LIBFABRIC.so` is present.
- Removes installer artifacts and APT lists after installation.
- Documents the behavior and records the new build arguments in
  `docker/versions.json`.

Duplicate-work checks found no open PR referencing issue #55635 or implementing
the same AWS EFA runtime support for KV connectors.

AI assistance disclosure: Codex was used to help inspect the relevant build
paths, implement the change, and prepare validation. I reviewed and understand
the submitted changes and can explain and maintain them.

## Test Plan

Local validation:

```bash
.venv/bin/python tools/generate_versions_json.py --check
SKIP=update-dockerfile-graph pre-commit run --files \
  docker/Dockerfile \
  docker/versions.json \
  docs/contributing/dockerfile/dockerfile.md
git diff --check
```

## Validation status

The current PR head is d8983e6f25f5b49500a317e9c1bd75a0ee9e9990. The Dockerfile and docker/versions.json pin AWS EFA installer 1.50.0 and its SHA-256 checksum. EFA userspace installation is enabled by INSTALL_KV_CONNECTORS=true; kernel modules and host limits remain host-managed.

@snadampal reported a successful local image build on September 17. Exact build provenance and end-to-end results are still pending. I have not independently built or published an image, and my AWS GPU/EFA quota request remains pending.

The earlier GitHub image build did not start because downstream jobs were gated by the pre-run check. A separate pre-commit failure remains unresolved.

Hardware validation remains pending: EFA provider discovery inside the container, NIXL LIBFABRIC transfers using GPU memory, and a small vLLM KV-connector end-to-end test. The reported build success does not establish these runtime results.

files.patch:
@@ -28,6 +28,8 @@ ARG UBUNTU_VERSION=24.04
 ARG INSTALL_RUBIN_PRERELEASE=false
 ARG TRITON_INSTALL_FROM_SOURCE_REPO=
 ARG TRITON_INSTALL_FROM_SOURCE_REVISION=
+ARG EFA_INSTALLER_VERSION=1.50.0
+ARG EFA_INSTALLER_SHA256=fa6dff8593d866866c13cb4640d9059835cd4efa427971f100ab40c97bef2841
 # DeepEPv2 requires NCCL >= 2.30.4 (GIN backend).
 # This version is used for CUDA 12+ builds to keep the DeepEP build and
 # runtime NCCL versions compatible.
@@ -1181,6 +1183,8 @@ RUN mv vllm src/vllm
 FROM vllm-base AS vllm-openai-base
 ARG TARGETPLATFORM
 ARG INSTALL_KV_CONNECTORS=false
+ARG EFA_INSTALLER_VERSION
+ARG EFA_INSTALLER_SHA256
 ARG INSTALL_RUBIN_PRERELEASE
 ARG TRITON_INSTALL_FROM_SOURCE_REPO
 ARG CUDA_VERSION
@@ -1229,6 +1233,46 @@ RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/opt/uv/cache \
         fi; \
     fi
 
+# Install the EFA userspace stack for NIXL's bundled LIBFABRIC plugin. Kernel
+# modules and host limits remain the responsibility of the container host.
+#
+# `set -eu` is required: this body is a `;`-separated sequence run by /bin/sh,
+# so without it only the final command decides the RUN exit status and a failed
+# install silently produces an empty layer.
+#
+# Note that efa_installer.sh replaces Ubuntu's libibverbs1/ibverbs-providers
+# with AWS's rdma-core build. That is deliberate -- the bundled libfabric needs
+# IBVERBS_1.18 and EFA_1.4-1.7, which Ubuntu's rdma-core does not export -- so
+# later layers must not reinstall the distro packages over it.
+RUN if [ "${INSTALL_KV_CONNECTORS}" = "true" ]; then \
+        set -eu; \
+        EFA_INSTALLER_ARCHIVE="/tmp/aws-efa-installer-${EFA_INSTALLER_VERSION}.tar.gz"; \
+        curl -fsSL --retry 3 --retry-all-errors \
+            "https://efa-installer.amazonaws.com/aws-efa-installer-${EFA_INSTALLER_VERSION}.tar.gz" \
+            -o "${EFA_INSTALLER_ARCHIVE}"; \
+        echo "${EFA_INSTALLER_SHA256}  ${EFA_INSTALLER_ARCHIVE}" \
+            | sha256sum -c -; \
+        tar -xzf "${EFA_INSTALLER_ARCHIVE}" -C /tmp; \
+        # efa_installer.sh apt-installs pciutils/environment-modules/tcl, and
+        # earlier layers purge /var/lib/apt/lists, so refresh the lists first.
+        apt-get update -y; \
+        # --minimal is not usable here: it installs rdma-core but skips
+        # libfabric, which is the only piece the LIBFABRIC plugin needs.
+        (cd /tmp/aws-efa-installer && \
+            ./efa_installer.sh -y --skip-kmod --skip-limit-conf --no-verify); \
+        test -x /opt/amazon/efa/bin/fi_info; \
+        /opt/amazon/efa/bin/fi_info --version; \
+        # Verify the plugin resolves libfabric at load time. Checking only that
+        # the file exists is useless: the NIXL wheel always ships the plugin,
+        # so that passes even when no libfabric is installed at all.
+        EFA_NIXL_PLUGIN=$(find /usr/local/lib -name libplugin_LIBFABRIC.so \
+            -print -quit); \
+        test -n "${EFA_NIXL_PLUGIN}"; \
+        ldd "${EFA_NIXL_PLUGIN}" | grep -q 'libfabric\.so\.1 => /'; \
+        rm -rf "${EFA_INSTALLER_ARCHIVE}" /tmp/aws-efa-installer \
+            /var/lib/apt/lists/*; \
+    fi
+
 # Mooncake registers GPU memory for RDMA via nvidia-peermem by default. Hosts
 # without that module loaded (e.g. GB200) must pass WITH_NVIDIA_PEERMEM=0 at run
 # time; see docs/features/mooncake_connector_usage.md. Deliberately not an ENV

@@ -24,6 +24,10 @@ The `extensions-build` stage can also produce an optional source-built Triton wheel. `vllm-openai-base` installs that wheel after its other Python dependencies so dependency resolution cannot restore an older Triton version. +When `INSTALL_KV_CONNECTORS=true`, `vllm-openai-base` also installs the pinned +AWS EFA userspace stack. The upstream installer detects amd64 or arm64 and +skips kernel-module and host-limit changes, which must remain host-managed. + >
